sentences.text:
The petitioner herein has
preferred the instant application for quashment of the proceeding being G.R. case no. 319 of 2009,
presently pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bidhannagar under
Section 406/420/120B of the Ipc.

The instant proceeding has already been culminated into a charge-sheet and while this High Court granted anticipatory bail to the petitioner, observed that the petitioner is only a mere employee of the company named and styled as "Assurgent Technology Solutions" and it was further observed that the petitioner himself was not paid his monthly salary.

He further submits that the co-accused,
Shibaji Sengupta @ Shivaji was also charge-sheeted in the present case and was on the same footing with that of the present petitioner, had filed an application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in CRR no. 1672 of 2013 and this court by a judgment and order dated 24.9.2024, was pleased to quash the impugned proceeding qua the aforesaid Shibaji Sengupta @
Shivaji.

He further submits that the allegations levelled in the complaint even if taken in its entirety,
does not constitute any offence of cheating or criminal breach of trust.

Furthermore, it is settled principle of law under Section 406/420 of the IPC are mutually exclusive and cannot be applicable together in any given facts and circumstances of the case and as such, further continuance of the instant proceeding will be mere abuse of process of the court.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the application is admitted.

Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of the application upon the State through the office of Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon the opposite party no. 2 by speed post intimating the next date of hearing and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.
Let the matter appear in the Monthly list of May, 2026 under the heading "Contested Application".
Learned counsel for the petitioner prays for stay of the impugned proceeding.

Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and that the petitioner had made out an arguable case which requires adjudication on merit, let all further proceedings being G.R. case no. 319 of 2009, presently pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bidhannagar be stayed for a period of twelve weeks or until further order, whichever is earlier.
Urgent Photostat certified copy of this order, duly applied for, be given to the parties upon compliance of all requisite formalities.
(Dr. Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J.)
